properties.name: Cherokee Nation
properties.notes: Traditional homelands in the southern Appalachians and Tennessee Valley.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma (Eastern Band remains in NC)

properties.name: Cherokee Nation
properties.notes: Forced to Indian Territory (present-day Oklahoma) via Trail of Tears. Eastern Band remained hidden in NC mountains.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma (Eastern Band remains in NC)

properties.name: Choctaw Nation
properties.notes: Homeland across central Mississippi and Alabama.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma (Mississippi Band remains in MS)

properties.name: Choctaw Nation
properties.notes: First nation removed under Indian Removal Act (1831–1833). Mississippi Band remained in homelands.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma (Mississippi Band remains in MS)

properties.name: Creek Nation (Muscogee)
properties.notes: Central Alabama and western Georgia.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma (Muscogee Nation)

properties.name: Creek Nation (Muscogee)
properties.notes: Removed to Indian Territory 1836–1837. Members who stayed were often violently attacked.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma (Muscogee Nation)

properties.name: Chickasaw Nation
properties.notes: Northern Mississippi, western Tennessee, parts of Kentucky and Alabama.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma

properties.name: Chickasaw Nation
properties.notes: Removed to Indian Territory (now south-central Oklahoma) starting 1837.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma

properties.name: Seminole Nation
properties.notes: Florida peninsula. Seminole people never formally surrendered. A portion remains in Florida to this day.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Seminole Nation of Oklahoma & Seminole Tribe of Florida

properties.name: Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina
properties.notes: Robeson County, North Carolina — the largest off-reservation Indian community in the Southeast.
properties.current_status: State Recognized (NC); Partial federal acknowledgment — pending full federal recognition

properties.name: Catawba Indian Nation
properties.notes: Piedmont region of the Carolinas. Maintained homeland through successive colonial and state pressure.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — South Carolina

properties.name: Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy)
properties.notes: Central and western New York. Portions of the original territory remain as reservations.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Six Nations

properties.name: Lenape (Delaware Nation)
properties.notes: Delaware Valley, New Jersey, and southeastern New York.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma; Delaware Tribe of Indians (KS)

properties.name: Lenape (Delaware Nation)
properties.notes: Gradually pushed west through Ohio, Indiana, Kansas, and eventually Oklahoma via a series of treaty removals.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma; Delaware Tribe of Indians (KS)

properties.name: Wampanoag Nation
properties.notes: Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard, and southeastern Massachusetts.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe; Wampanoag Tribe of Gay Head (Aquinnah)

properties.name: Ojibwe / Chippewa Nation
properties.notes: Great Lakes region extending into the northern Plains. Wild rice (manoomin) homeland.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — multiple bands across MN, WI, MI, ND, MT

properties.name: Menominee Indian Tribe
properties.notes: Green Bay region and the Menominee River Valley, Wisconsin.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Wisconsin

properties.name: Potawatomi Nation
properties.notes: Lake Michigan shoreline and the Chicago region. The word 'Chicago' derives from a Potawatomi/Algonquian term.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — multiple bands in MI, KS, OK, WI

properties.name: Potawatomi Nation
properties.notes: Trail of Death (1838) forced removal to Kansas. Multiple subsequent removals to Oklahoma.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — multiple bands in MI, KS, OK, WI

properties.name: Lakota / Sioux Nation
properties.notes: Northern Great Plains. The Black Hills (He Sapa) are the Lakota sacred homeland.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — multiple bands (Standing Rock, Cheyenne River, Rosebud, Pine Ridge, etc.)

properties.name: Cheyenne Nation
properties.notes: Wyoming and Colorado high plains. Later shared range with Arapaho.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Northern Cheyenne (MT) and Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes (OK)

properties.name: Cheyenne Nation
properties.notes: Northern Cheyenne returned to Montana against federal orders. Southern Cheyenne removed to Indian Territory (Oklahoma).
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Northern Cheyenne (MT) and Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes (OK)

properties.name: Osage Nation
properties.notes: Southern Missouri and northern Arkansas, later Kansas.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Osage Nation, Oklahoma

properties.name: Osage Nation
properties.notes: Osage County, Oklahoma — site of early 20th-century oil discovery and the Reign of Terror.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Osage Nation, Oklahoma

properties.name: Comanche Nation
properties.notes: Comanchería — a vast territory across the Southern Plains, controlled by the Comanche until 1875.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma

properties.name: Comanche Nation
properties.notes: Confined to Fort Sill area of Oklahoma following Red River War.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oklahoma

properties.name: Navajo Nation (Diné Bikéyah)
properties.notes: Four Corners region. The Long Walk (1864) removed Navajo to Fort Sumner but they returned in 1868 after the Treaty of Bosque Redondo guaranteed their homeland.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — largest reservation in the United States

properties.name: Apache Nations
properties.notes: Arizona, New Mexico, west Texas, and northern Mexico. Multiple bands maintained distinct territories.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — multiple Apache nations in AZ, NM, OK

properties.name: Tohono O'odham Nation
properties.notes: Sonoran Desert of southern Arizona and northern Sonora (Mexico). The international border bisects their traditional territory.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — second largest reservation land area in the US

properties.name: Nez Perce Tribe
properties.notes: Wallowa Valley (Oregon) and Clearwater River region (Idaho).
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Idaho

properties.name: Nez Perce Tribe
properties.notes: After the 1877 war, confined to smaller Idaho reservation. Some ended up in Oklahoma, then returned to Idaho.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Idaho

properties.name: Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation
properties.notes: Columbia Plateau and Cascade Mountain region. Yakama Treaty of 1855 guaranteed fishing, hunting, and gathering rights.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Washington

properties.name: Yurok Tribe
properties.notes: Klamath River and Pacific Coast of Northern California. The Klamath River is their cultural and spiritual center.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Northern California

properties.name: Chumash Nation
properties.notes: Southern California coastal region from Malibu to Paso Robles, including the Channel Islands.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians

properties.name: Pueblo Nations (New Mexico)
properties.notes: Rio Grande Valley and western New Mexico. Home to some of the oldest continuously occupied settlements in North America.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — 19 Pueblos in New Mexico

properties.name: Ute Nation
properties.notes: Entire Colorado and Utah plateau region.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Ute Indian Tribe (UT), Southern Ute (CO), Ute Mountain Ute (CO)

properties.name: Ute Nation
properties.notes: Confined to smaller reservations in southwestern Colorado and northeastern Utah after the Meeker Massacre and subsequent forced removal.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Ute Indian Tribe (UT), Southern Ute (CO), Ute Mountain Ute (CO)

properties.name: Paiute Nation
properties.notes: Great Basin desert region across Nevada, California, Oregon, Utah, and Idaho.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — multiple bands (Northern, Southern, Owens Valley)

properties.name: Shoshone Nation
properties.notes: Great Basin and Rocky Mountain region. Sacagawea was Lemhi Shoshone.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — multiple bands

properties.name: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians
properties.notes: Qualla Boundary, Western North Carolina. Never removed. Tsali and others hid in the mountains during the Trail of Tears.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Western North Carolina

properties.name: Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians
properties.notes: East-central Mississippi. Never left their homeland despite the 1830 Indian Removal Act.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Mississippi

properties.name: Penobscot Indian Nation
properties.notes: Penobscot River watershed in Maine. The river is named for the nation.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Maine

properties.name: Oneida Nation
properties.notes: Central New York. Oneida Nation is pressing major land claims in New York under the Non-Intercourse Act.
properties.current_status: Federally Recognized — Oneida Indian Nation (NY), Oneida Nation (WI)
